sentences.text: Plioperdix is an extinct genus belonging to the family Phasianidae, a group of birds that includes modern pheasants and partridges.
The extinct genus Plioperdix was formally described by Kretzoi in 1955.
This animal lived during the Neogene period, specifically between 8.725 and 5.09 million years ago, spanning the Tortonian to Zanclean ages.
Fossils of Plioperdix ponticus have been found in Moldova, southern Ukraine, Transbaikalia, Mongolia, and Morocco, while Plioperdix hungarica is known from the Late Miocene of Hungary and Russia.
It is currently debated whether Plioperdix hungarica represents a valid species within the genus Plioperdix.
